h1: Google Maps Know Before You Go Tips: What Restaurants Should Know
answer: Google Maps know before you go tips are insider notes from the Maps community, shown when people search for restaurants, cafes and diners, covering things like how to get a reservation, where to park and what to order. Google highlighted them in October 2026 with Ask Maps and weekly dining lists. Anaheim and Orange County restaurants can shape these tips through clear information and good guest experiences.
key_takeaways: Tips come from the Maps community.
They cover reservations, parking and dishes.
Ask Maps analyzes photos, reviews and menus.
Clear information helps guests leave useful tips.

sections.heading: What Google highlighted
sections.body_html: On October 8, 2026, Google shared three Google Maps features for finding a meal: Ask Maps for finding and ordering what people crave, trending dining lists in the Explore tab and know before you go tips from the Maps community.

sections.heading: Know before you go tips
sections.body_html: Google says that when people search for restaurants, cafes and diners, they can scroll down to find insider tips from the Maps community, including how to get a hard-to-get reservation, where to park and which dishes to order.

sections.heading: Ask Maps
sections.body_html: Google says people can say or type what they want, such as fall dessert spots with outdoor seating, and Ask Maps analyzes billions of photos, reviews and menus to find a match. It can also let people order delivery through partners like Uber Eats, Toast and Square.

sections.heading: Trending dining lists
sections.body_html: The Explore tab shows dining lists updated weekly, according to Google: Trending for places that recently spiked in popularity, Gems for new neighborhood favorites and Top for tried-and-true classics. People can save them with a tap.

sections.heading: Why these features matter
sections.body_html: Each feature draws on information about your restaurant that comes from guests and from you: photos, reviews, menus and community tips. Restaurants that make the basics easy to understand, from parking to signature dishes, give diners and Maps more useful details to share.

sections.heading: Make parking and arrival easy
sections.body_html: Parking is one of the tip topics Google mentions. Put clear parking and arrival details on your website and Business Profile, such as validated parking, the nearest lot or the best entrance. Near the Anaheim Resort and busy Orange County centers, this makes a real difference.

sections.heading: Be clear about reservations
sections.body_html: If you take reservations, explain how far ahead they open, whether you hold tables for walk-ins and how to join a waitlist. Clear rules mean guests share accurate tips rather than guesses.

sections.heading: Make your signature dishes obvious
sections.body_html: Diners often tell others what to order. Name your signature dishes on the menu, in photos and on your website, and keep your menu as text, so the dishes guests mention match what Maps can find.

sections.heading: What restaurants can do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Check your Business Profile menu, hours and photos.
  2. Add parking and arrival details.
  3. Explain reservations and waitlists.
  4. Upload photos of signature dishes.
  5. Reply to recent reviews.
  6. Check ordering links work.

sections.heading: Don't try to game tips
sections.body_html: Tips and reviews should come from real guests. Asking staff or friends to post fake tips or reviews breaks Google's policies and erodes trust. Focus on giving real guests a great experience and clear information.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a ramen shop in Tustin where guests often struggle to find parking. The owner adds clear parking directions to the website and Business Profile, posts photos of the three most popular bowls and explains the walk-in waitlist. Over the following weeks, guest tips mention the parking lot behind the building and the spicy miso ramen.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether they can edit know before you go tips. They come from the Maps community, so the best influence is clear information and good experiences. Another common question is how to get into trending lists. Google describes them as based on popularity and favorites, so there's no shortcut; steady visits, reviews and photos help. Owners also ask whether Ask Maps ordering needs a specific partner. Google names partners like Uber Eats, Toast and Square for delivery orders.

sections.heading: Train staff to share the right details
sections.body_html: Front-of-house staff answer the same questions every day: where to park, how long the wait is, which dishes are popular and whether there's outdoor seating. Write short, accurate answers to these questions and share them with the team, so guests hear the same information whoever they ask. Guests who get clear, consistent answers are more likely to pass them on in tips and reviews. Update the answers when anything changes, such as a new parking arrangement or a seasonal menu, and add them to your website's visit page at the same time.

sections.heading: Use your Business Profile as the source of truth
sections.body_html: Your Google Business Profile is where you control the facts: name, hours, menu, photos, attributes like outdoor seating and reservation or ordering links. Keep it complete and current, especially holiday hours in November and December. Add new photos of dishes and the dining room every month, and reply to reviews in a friendly, specific way. When your own information is clear and accurate, guest tips tend to build on it rather than correct it, and Ask Maps has better material to match your restaurant to what people are searching for.

sections.heading: Watch what guests say
sections.body_html: Read the tips and reviews guests leave about your restaurant every few weeks. They often reveal small problems you can fix, such as confusing parking, a hard-to-find entrance or long waits at certain times, and the dishes people love most. Treat them as free feedback. If several guests mention the same issue, fix it and update your information. If they rave about a dish, feature it in photos and on the menu. Over time, this loop between guest feedback and your own information improves both the experience and how your restaurant appears on Maps.

sections.heading: Prepare for busy nights and events
sections.body_html: Orange County restaurants near stadiums, convention venues and the resort area see sudden rushes on event nights. Guests often leave tips about these nights, such as arriving early or booking ahead. Get ahead of them by posting event-night details on your Business Profile and website: expected waits, reservation advice, parking changes and any special menus. Guests who know what to expect have a better experience, and the tips they leave afterwards are more likely to be helpful and positive rather than complaints about surprises they could have avoided with a little more information from you.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Google Maps know before you go tips, trending lists and Ask Maps all draw on real information about your restaurant. Anaheim and Orange County restaurants that make parking, reservations and signature dishes clear, and keep menus and photos current, give diners and Maps better material to recommend them.
